timing: Specified after persistent stable-adjustment-cost models failed, before computing aggregate persistent purposeful-repricing bounds. Extends the previously studied daily no-harm comparison, not a newly selected numerical tolerance.
motivation: A stable K and every-review decision restrictions may fail even when deliberate repricing improves contribution in aggregate. Do not infer anything about ignored changes.
restriction: Actual persistent-review contribution >= retaining previous fresh quotes in aggregate; nonnegative actual contribution. Both seller-pooled and separately-by-phone-model versions. Unknown unrestricted nonnegative persistent listing costs. No adjustment cost or epsilon fitted.
payoffs_and_horizons: Exactly the three demand fits and five horizon laws in gadgetpickup_persistent_review_design_20261020.json; reuse its predictions, eligibility, survival probabilities and review-exposure target.
guarantee_scope: Zero aggregate regret only against the specified rollback of implemented changes, as a maintained economic assumption. Not an empirically measured zero loss, a bound against unimplemented shifts, or an ANR finite-sample theorem.
reporting: Report all horizons/fits/groupings whether useful, empty, or broad. No causal demand confidence claims. Retain the original realized-sales target as unresolved.
